relationships.title: Re: out brief and next steps from our meeting with YT
relationships.evidence:
Please all let us all your thoughts on priority countries. My thinking is we pick from bright spots, where there's
opportunity for programming related to disinformation and digital auth AND some related SP's travels. I think
Eastern Europe, Indonesia, and some in LAC (is Brazil) could be interesting from DRG angle, plus Kenya and
India, where SP is heading in not too distant future.
Also, I'm happy to loop LPA for coms engagement with You Tube.
Cheers! V
On Wed, Jul 6, 2022 at 8:55 AM Joshua Machleder <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks Vera for sending out.
One question that has some urgency to it is Josh's proposed pilot for working with "Creator Cohorts" in a region,
which is something that he'd like to do by December 31, 2022. This would require some early action on our part,
including a series of decision points in terms of the where: what are the USAID priority countries/regions, where
is there an existing (media and/or civil society) activity that this could be paired with, what Mission(s) are willing
to put in the extra work to do this (and their implementing partners as well).
I can casually begin some exploratory discussions with some Missions to gauge interest and realism, but look to
you for guidance on where we may want to focus.
Best,
josh
On Tue, Jul 5, 2022 at 10:50 PM Vera Zakem <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Hi All,
Last week, Josh and I met with Josh Blumenfeld from YT to see how we can partner with YouTube on a
number of initiatives. This was a follow up meeting that the Administrator had with Susan Wojcicki. I wanted to
share the BLUF and next steps (thanks to JM for capturing!)
• Josh Blumenfeld will be our primary POC there for all things related to removing content to proactive
engagement.
• "Trusted Flaggers:" YouTube is looking for "trusted flaggers" to be a part of their program. "Trusted
flaggers" are groups that assist in YouTube's content moderation process and provide insight on local
context and language, identifying problematic content that YouTube or its automated systems would not
necessarily catch. Decision: We should ID a list of priority countries that are relevant to USAID, where
we can help identify local partners to participate in YouTube's "trusted flagger" partner programs and
contacts at Missions, Implementing Partners, Local Partners. (Initial suggestions may include: A/AID
priority countries, bright spots, countries where DRG will be supporting elections.)
• YouTube proposes the following partnerships with USAID:
• Trainings for USAID communicators (i.e. FO, LPA, and DOCs) on effective use of YouTube- is
this of interest? Can we set this up? I can reach out to LPA
• "Creator Cohorts:" Supporting a cohort of YouTube creators and or media outlets that use
YouTube with equipment and training. Josh will draft up a short concept for us to flesh out that
proposes a co-branded, potentially regional program convening of a group of approximately 25
creators/journalists that could be provided with startup funds, equipment, and training on
YouTube's backend analytics. YouTube would like to do this before the end of this calendar
year. Decision: potential ideas for co-branded programs may include a partnership between
existing USAID media/civil society programming with YouTube to support a regional cohort of
creators receiving training and startup funds. Johnny / Troika - thoughts? Initial ideas for pilots
are:
• Ukraine, Moldova, Belarus, where USAID has robust media programs that also include
support to creators as well as newsrooms that include YouTube in their business model
• RDMA where USAID is launching a regional activity to support fact checkers
• LAC where USAID has a regional investigative journalism program (PROSAFE)
• They would like to use opportunities of Administrator's travels in the field to set up interviews
with YouTube creators from those countries. Also, UNGA could be an idea. Adam - thoughts?
